title: Stock market basics — demat account, risk and how not to lose money
publisher: Artha Kavach summary of public guidance (RBI / SEBI / IRDAI / Income Tax Dept) — pending manual verification
text: Buying a share makes you a part-owner of a company. To buy and sell listed shares you need a demat account and a trading account with a SEBI-registered broker, plus KYC. Share prices move daily and can fall 30–50% in a bad year, so only money you will not need for 5+ years should be in stocks. Most beginners do better with diversified index or flexi-cap funds than picking single stocks; if you do pick stocks, limit it to a small share of your portfolio and never invest borrowed money. Be wary of 'tips' from social media, Telegram or WhatsApp groups promising quick profits — these are the most common route for investment scams. Check that a broker or adviser is registered on sebi.gov.in before giving them any money, and never share your demat or trading login or OTP.
summary_hinglish: Share kharidne ke liye SEBI-registered broker ke saath demat aur trading account chahiye. Shares ek saal mein 30-50% gir sakte hain, isliye sirf wahi paisa lagao jo 5+ saal nahi chahiye. Beginners ke liye index/diversified funds aksar behtar hain. Telegram/WhatsApp ke tips se bacho, broker ka SEBI registration check karo.
summary_hi: शेयर खरीदने के लिए SEBI-पंजीकृत ब्रोकर के साथ डीमैट और ट्रेडिंग खाता चाहिए। शेयर एक साल में 30-50% गिर सकते हैं, इसलिए सिर्फ वही पैसा लगाएं जो 5+ साल नहीं चाहिए। शुरुआती लोगों के लिए इंडेक्स/डाइवर्सिफाइड फंड अक्सर बेहतर हैं। टेलीग्राम/व्हाट्सऐप टिप्स से बचें।
